summary: All four compliance gates cleared. Data originates from a U.S. federal open-data portal with no authentication barrier; contains only facility-level business-contact fields and regulatory identifiers with zero patient records; commercial resale of formatted U.S. government data is well-established and legally sound; and HIPAA does not apply because no individually identifiable health information is present. Clear to ship.

public_data_source.rationale: Dataset sourced exclusively from CMS Provider Data Catalog (https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/dataset/6jpm-sxkc). CMS.gov is operated by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, a U.S. federal agency. The dataset is freely downloadable with no login, no paywall, no API key, and no rate-limiting access control. The opportunity brief confirms source_rights.public = true and lists three corroborating CMS URLs. Every row carries a source_url pointing back to the CMS catalog, satisfying the hard rule of source traceability.

pii_assessment.rationale: All 15 columns are facility-level or regulatory fields. There are no personal names, personal email addresses, Social Security Numbers, dates of birth, personal home addresses, or any other field that identifies a natural person. The data-steward validation independently confirmed pii_ssn: PASS and pii_personal_email: PASS across all 12,392 rows. Phone numbers are business lines published by CMS as part of the provider record, not personal mobile numbers. Business addresses are registered facility locations. These are standard B2B contact fields that do not constitute PII under any current U.S. or EU privacy standard in a B2B context.

commercial_resale_rights.rationale: Works produced by officers or employees of the U.S. federal government as part of their official duties are in the public domain under 17 U.S.C. § 105 — no copyright attaches. CMS is a federal agency; this dataset is a direct product of its statutory mandate to publish Medicare provider information. The data.cms.gov portal publishes under an open-data policy with no restriction on downstream commercial use. Established market precedent confirms legality: CarePrecise charges $859–$4,795/year for a database built from the same CMS/NPPES/PECOS sources; Ampliz charges $50/month for similar formatted healthcare provider data. These companies have operated commercially on this model for years without legal challenge. No terms-of-service clause on data.cms.gov prohibits commercial redistribution.

hipaa.rationale: HIPAA's Privacy Rule (45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164) protects 'Protected Health Information' (PHI) — individually identifiable health information relating to a patient's past, present, or future physical or mental health or condition, or the provision of or payment for health care to an individual. This dataset contains zero patient records. Every row is a Medicare-certified home health agency (a business entity), not a patient. Fields such as quality star ratings are aggregate facility-performance scores published by CMS; they are not derived from or linked to any individual's health record in this dataset. CMS itself publishes this data publicly, which would be impermissible if it constituted PHI. DataStructured is not a covered entity or business associate under HIPAA, and this dataset does not trigger HIPAA obligations.

notes: 490 rows (3.95%) have null phone — expected; CMS source data is incomplete for some agencies. Not a compliance issue.
2,037 rows (16.44%) have null ownership_type — CMS source gap. Not a compliance issue.
4,431 rows (35.76%) have null overall_quality_star_rating — CMS assigns ratings only to agencies that have submitted sufficient quality data. Not a compliance issue.
No rows have null source_url — hard provenance requirement satisfied 100%.
